title: A shrinking charge-analytic radius controls both full-PDE leakage terms and yields finite-tier cutoff Cauchy control

hierarchy.coefficient: For smooth cutoff solutions set B(t)=1+||E(t)||_(H2)+||phi(t)||_(H2)||D_t phi(t)||_(H2)
hierarchy.one_step_inequality: Sobolev H2 embeds in L-infinity on T3. K1413 therefore gives |dF_n/dt|<=C B(t)(F_n+sqrt(F_n F_(n+1))) with C independent of the charge cutoff: the radial term uses ||partial_t||phi||^2||_infinity and the current uses ||E||_infinity
hierarchy.analytic_energy: For rho>0 define G_rho=sum_(n>=0) rho^(2n) F_n/n! and D_rho=sum_(n>=1) n rho^(2n)F_n/n!
hierarchy.shift_identity: sum_n a_n sqrt(F_nF_(n+1))<=G_rho/2+D_rho/(2rho^2), because a_(n-1)=n a_n/rho^2
hierarchy.shrinking_radius: Choose R(t)=rho(t)^2 with R'(t)=-C B(t). While R(t)>0, the negative weight derivative absorbs D_rho/(rho^2) and G_(rho(t))(t)<=G_(rho(0))(0) exp(C integral_0^t B)
hierarchy.finite_tier_cauchy: For every sigma<rho(t) and fixed charge tier n, the exponential spectral tail implied by sum exp(rho(t)^2 q^2) times the mode energy, together with K1396's local Lipschitz difference estimate, makes charge-spectral cutoff solutions Cauchy at tier n on the interval
hierarchy.ceiling: This is cutoff-uniform nonlinear control conditional on a common integrable H2 coefficient and positive analytic radius. It neither proves those hypotheses globally nor constructs a global completed flow, null-form decay, source selector, or physical cohomology
